collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE I: SONGS, CHANTS, SPEECHES AND WELCOMES (LCA-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
Isola sings, chants and speaks for itself: welcoming a new leader, wishing travelers luck, greeting newcomers and newborns, rallying for hard work, standing up for each other, and arguing about who gets the next verse.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: The fishers have an old call-and-response across the water: teach it to a newcomer, or keep it among the crews.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: When the canoes are far apart on the water, the fishers call to each other in an old call-and-response: one canoe calls, the others answer, and everyone knows where everyone is. (friend) is new to the crews and does not know the calls. (subject) is not sure the calls should be taught to anyone who has not fished for a full season. What should (subject) do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) teaches (friend) the calls in a single afternoon on the beach. (friend) gets one wrong on (friend.his/her) first trip and three canoes paddle over to rescue (friend.him/her) from a danger that does not exist. Everyone thinks it is hilarious. (friend) never gets it wrong again.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) tells (friend) to fish one full season first, the way everyone did. (friend) is stung, but agrees. All season (friend.he/she) listens to the calls and learns them on (friend.his/her) own. At the end of the season, (friend.he/she) answers (subject)'s call perfectly before anyone has taught (friend.him/her) a thing.
